title: Orphaned vault value after last relinquishPrincipal: relinquishing until totalDeposited==0 while getTotalShares()>0 freezes residual value, capturable in full by the next single depositor's skim
description: relinquishPrincipal decrements totalDeposited (and clientBalances) without disposing the backing vault shares (this share-untouched write-down is intended per IYieldStrategy NatSpec L34-41). When the LAST principal is relinquished, totalDeposited reaches 0 while getTotalShares() > 0, so the residual vault value becomes un-attributable. _skimSurplus early-returns on totalDeposited==0, FREEZING the residual. The instant fresh principal re-enters, a single depositor's totalBalanceOf = totalValue*principal/totalDeposited momentarily inflates to the entire residual position, and the following skimSurplus delivers the full residual to that recipient (a protocol-owned, owner-curated client — not an external attacker). Adjacent but distinct from QA-08 (skim-de-buffering discount-cushion footgun, different root cause) and from M-02/L-01 (NAV/slippage).
impact: Mis-attribution / sequencing hazard: residual yield value can be captured in full by whoever deposits first after a full relinquish-to-zero. NO value creation — the Tier-3 value-conservation invariant holds (128k-call fuzz across both in-scope concrete strategies); this is internal redistribution inside the protocol's own books, not insolvency and not a leak to an external party. Non-obvious operational footgun (Law 3) for the owner/integrator sequencing relinquish-to-zero with live residual shares.
attackPath: 1. (Privileged, self-inflicted) The LAST remaining authorized client calls relinquishPrincipal repeatedly (or the owner calls relinquishPrincipalAsOwner) until clientBalances and totalDeposited reach 0 while getTotalShares() > 0 (shares deliberately untouched by relinquish).
2. The residual vault value is now orphaned and FROZEN: _skimSurplus early-returns while totalDeposited == 0, so no skim can distribute it.
3. A fresh deposit re-enters principal; that single depositor's totalBalanceOf = (totalValue * principal)/totalDeposited momentarily reflects the ENTIRE residual position.
4. A subsequent skimSurplus delivers the full residual to the recipient/next-depositor — who is a protocol-owned, owner-curated client (setClient is onlyOwner), NOT an external attacker.
lawBasis: Law-3 non-obvious owner/integrator footgun. Surprise test PASSES: a competent, non-malicious integrator sequencing relinquish-to-zero with live residual shares would be surprised that the residual is frozen and then handed in full to the first re-depositor. Parked visibly per Law-1 (no silent drop); reported as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance, NOT as a malicious-owner vector.
documentationCheck: NOT-BLESSED. IYieldStrategy NatSpec (L34-41) blesses the share-untouched write-down and value-to-yield re-attribution 'ON RECOVERY' but presumes a surviving recovery path (a remaining client); it does NOT document the totalDeposited==0-with-shares orphan + re-capture-on-redeposit edge. No designDecision (incl. #2 requested-not-received, a WITHDRAW-path rule) and no systemAssumption covers it. knownIssuesCount=0.
recommendation: Either dispose/redeem the proportional vault shares on relinquish, or prevent totalDeposited from reaching 0 while getTotalShares() > 0 (sweep/attribute the residual to a protocol sink), or document the sequencing hazard with safe-config guidance so an integrator never relinquishes-to-zero while live residual shares remain.
